title: Cohomology commutes with finite products of complexes of abelian groups
statement: Let $I$ be a finite set and, for each $i\in I$, let $K_i^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of abelian groups [def-sp-abelian]. The componentwise product complex $K^\bullet=\prod_{i\in I}K_i^\bullet$ has canonical natural isomorphisms $\mathcal H^q(K^\bullet)\cong\prod_{i\in I}\mathcal H^q(K_i^\bullet)$ for every integer $q$.

source.place: elementary homology of finite products of complexes; formulation supplied by the worker

proof.text: For each degree q, the differential of the componentwise product complex is the product of the differentials. Therefore its q-cycles are exactly the tuples of q-cycles, $Z^q(K)=\prod_{i\in I}Z^q(K_i)$, and its q-boundaries are exactly the tuples of q-boundaries, $B^q(K)=\prod_{i\in I}B^q(K_i)$: membership is checked coordinatewise, and for the reverse inclusion choose a preimage in each coordinate (only finitely many choices are required).

source.place: elementary homology of finite products of complexes; formulation supplied by the worker

proof.text: The coordinate quotient maps induce a homomorphism $Z^q(K)/B^q(K)\to\prod_{i\in I}(Z^q(K_i)/B^q(K_i))$. It is injective because a tuple of cycles maps to zero exactly when each coordinate is a boundary, hence the tuple is in $\prod_iB^q(K_i)=B^q(K)$; it is surjective by choosing representatives of each coordinate class and assembling them into one tuple. Thus it is the canonical isomorphism $\mathcal H^q(K)\cong\prod_i\mathcal H^q(K_i)$. Every construction uses coordinate projections and commutes with a morphism of complexes, so these isomorphisms are natural in the family and in q.
